subject: K-means clustering, constrain cluster assignment with dir(0.1, ..., 0.1)

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: K-means clustering, constrain cluster assignment with dir(0.1, ..., 0.1)
parts:
Hello,

the model I am referring to is https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/tree/master/misc/cluster/soft-k-means

I have a problem of assignment of single observations to one of three normal distributions.I know how many observations there are in each distribution. So I would like to force observations that are similarly distant from a centroid to compete for the assignment.

For doing this, I though that adding a Dirichlet prior with hyperparameter > 0 < 1 would force the model to take a guess either 0 or 1. Does this make sense or it is too "creative"?

If it makes sense then the fact that the prediction is done on UNnormalized soft_z is a problem because is hard to convert to simplex (for being compatible to dirichlet prior).

I hope you can shed some light about this issue :)
Thanks.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] K-means clustering, constrain cluster assignment with dir(0.1, ..., 0.1)
parts:
If you look at the conjugate posterior, you'll see that the Dirichlet
is very weak if you have data in each bin.

But I'm not sure what you mean by "you know how many observations there
are in each distribution". You want to think generatively rather than trying
to hack the model. Does it mean you know the mixing distribution?
If so, just fix that. If not, what does it mean?

I didn't understand what you meant by soft_z.

- Bob

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: K-means clustering, constrain cluster assignment with dir(0.1, ..., 0.1)
parts:
Yes, this works... in theory.
What you're doing is something I've played with for a while: Encouraging high probability clustering by using betas and dirichlets with parameters < 1. The closer to 0, the more probability mass is placed over the extremes.
You can then say each individual has a probability, pi_i, of belonging to each cluster, where pi_i ~ dirichlet(alphas), and alphas ~ dirichlet(.1,.1,.1,...), which gives you not only individual membership probabilities, but overall membership probabilities too (as well as shrinkage).

However, HMC/NUTS is simulating a particle across the posterior surface. Sampling from betas and dirichlets where the parameters are < 1 pushes the probability mass toward the edges of the constraint. When inverted, it looks like a plateau, and the particle simulation can hit some difficulties, causing divergent transitions.
All that to say: If you want to encourage categorization with high probabilities, reparameterize your model to sample log-odds parameters (logistic regression, softmax regression) and convert to probability for the likelihood. If you do this, you can get a similar effect to 'inverted betas and dirichlets' by simply making the logistic prior very wide, such that most of the probability mass is beyond 1 and -1.
